'''Julia Rosolovsky Greer''' is a [[materials scientist]] and is the [[Ruben F. Mettler|Ruben F. and Donna Mettler]] Professor of Materials Science, [[Mechanics]] and [[Biomedical engineering|Medical Engineering]] at the [[California Institute of Technology|California Institute of Technology (Caltech)]]. As of 2019, Greer is also the director of the [[Kavli Foundation (United States)|Kavli]] Nanoscience Institute at Caltech.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Julia Greer Named KNI Director {{!}} The Kavli Nanoscience Institute at Caltech |url=http://kni.caltech.edu/news/greer-kni-director |access-date=2023-02-02 |website=kni.caltech.edu}}</ref>

As a pioneer in the field of [[nanomechanics]] and architected materials, Greer has earned many awards, such as being named a CNN 2020 Visionary, for her work investigating how materials behave at the nano-scale.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Innovator Under 35: Julia Greer, 32 |url=http://www2.technologyreview.com/tr35/profile.aspx?TRID=708 |access-date=2019-03-06 |website=MIT Technology Review |language=en-us |archive-date=2018-11-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181111170908/http://www2.technologyreview.com/tr35/profile.aspx?trid=708 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="ONeill2016">{{Cite web|url=https://money.cnn.com/gallery/technology/2016/03/08/innovators-shaping-our-world/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310102355/http://money.cnn.com/gallery/technology/2016/03/08/innovators-shaping-our-world/|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 10, 2016|title=From carbon dioxide to chemotherapy: These innovators could change the world|last=O'Neill|first=Maggie|date=2016-03-08|website=CNNMoney|access-date=2019-03-07}}</ref> Greer has been a professor at Caltech since 2007, and is also an associate editor at both Extreme Mechanics Letters and [[Nano Letters]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Caltech Division of Engineering and Applied Science {{!}} Julia R. Greer |url=http://eas.caltech.edu/people/jrgreer |access-date=2019-03-04 |website=eas.caltech.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=J. R. Greer |url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/extreme-mechanics-letters/editorial-board/j-r-greer |access-date=2019-03-04 |website=www.journals.elsevier.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/nalefd/editors.html|title=Editors|website=pubs.acs.org|access-date=2019-03-04}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Greer was born in Moscow, Russia, and moved to the U.S. with her parents at the age of 16.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://sanmarinotribune.com/rollerblading-through-life/|title=Rollerblading Through Life|date=2016-10-06|website=San Marino Tribune|language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-06}}</ref> Greer attended the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)]] for college, where she received a Bachelors of Science in [[Chemical engineering|Chemical Engineering]] and a minor in Advanced Music Performance in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iinano.org/iin-frontiers-in-nanotechnology-seminar-series-julia-greer|title=IIN Frontiers in Nanotechnology Seminar Series - Julia Greer {{!}} International Institute for Nanotechnology|website=www.iinano.org|access-date=2019-03-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spectrum.mit.edu/continuum/five-from-mit-make-fast-companys-100-most-creative-people-in-business-for-2014/|title=Five from MIT Make Fast Company's 100 Most Creative People in Business for 2014|website=MIT Spectrum|language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-06}}</ref> Greer then went on to receive graduate degrees in Materials Science and Engineering; she earned a Masters of Science (M.S.) in 2000 and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in 2005, both from [[Stanford University]]. Between receiving her M.S. and Ph.D., Greer worked at [[Intel]] from 2000 to 2003.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Gewin|first=Virginia|date=2012-12-19|title=Turning point: Julia Greer|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=492|issue=7429|pages=459|doi=10.1038/nj7429-459a|issn=0028-0836|doi-access=free}}</ref> For her dissertation, titled "Size dependence of strength of gold at the micron scale in the absence of strain gradients,"<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://searchworks.stanford.edu/view/6260889|title=Size dependence of strength of gold at the micron scale in the absence of strain gradients|last=Rosolovsky Greer|first=Julia |year=2005 |bibcode=2005PhDT........94G |access-date=2019-03-06}}</ref> Greer worked with materials scientist [https://mse.stanford.edu/people/william-nix William D. Nix] studying the mechanical properties of nanopillars.<ref name=":2" /> After her PhD, Greer pursued postdoctoral studies at the [[Palo Alto Research Center|Palo Alto Research Center (PARC)]] from 2005 to 2007.

== Research and career ==
Greer joined the Materials Science Department at Caltech in 2007 as an assistant professor; she received tenure and was promoted to full professor in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ms.caltech.edu/people/jrgreer|title=Caltech Materials Science {{!}} Julia R. Greer|website=ms.caltech.edu|access-date=2019-03-06}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.weforum.org/people/julia-r-greer/|title=Julia Greer|website=World Economic Forum|access-date=2019-03-06}}</ref> Her research focuses on the application of nanotechnology in biomedical materials, multi-functional devices, energy storage, and material synthesis.

Greer has received much recognition and several career awards for her work. Her lab's early work has resulted in a new direction in nanomechanics.<ref name=":2" /> Her lab is now harnessing strategies in nanofabrication for applications ranging from improving lithium-ion batteries to developing biomedical devices.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stemgemsbook.com/bigger-doesnt-always-mean-stronger-julia-greer-is-changing-the-idea-of-how-materials-are-made/|title=Bigger Doesn't Always Mean Stronger: Julia Greer is Changing the Idea of How Materials Are Made|last=Espy|first=Stephanie|website=STEM Gems|date=17 May 2016 |language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-07}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In addition to being a scientist, Greer is also an accomplished pianist. She took piano lessons starting at age 5 and has studied music at several institutions, including Moscow's [[Gnessin State Musical College|Gnessin School of Music]], the [[Eastman School of Music]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], the [[San Francisco Conservatory of Music]], and [[Stanford University]].<ref name=":0" />

Greer also loves rollerblading. She will occasionally rollerblade to and from work and has even participated in a rollerblading marathon.<ref name=":0" />
